$comment: The one pinned tool table for every repo on the baseline, and the only file in shared-workflows a version is edited in. `tools` is what check-tool-versions checks, here and in every consumer: match 'exact' means the whole version must agree; 'major' means only the major, for runtimes pinned loosely on purpose. `mise` and `shell` are shared-workflows' own: scripts/self/render-versions.mjs --write generates the [tools] block of its .mise.toml from `mise`, in order, and scripts/lib/versions.sh (with the package's copy, lib/versions.sh) from `shell`, in order. An entry with `tool` takes that tool's version from `tools`, so it is written once; an entry with `version` (mise) or `value` (shell) pins something only shared-workflows uses. `comment` lines are written above the entry, an empty line as a bare '#'. `make check-version-pins` fails when a generated file has drifted from this one.

comment: label-sarif.sh and release-pr-read.sh need jq (require_cmd jq), and so does a
workflow-shape test, which fails without it rather than skipping.
This repo ships no package.json, but a dozen of its scripts shell out to pnpm
on the consumer's behalf - run-script.sh, web-export.sh, playwright.sh,
expo-config.sh - and their tests exercise those paths. Without pnpm on PATH
every one of them fails `require_cmd pnpm`, which is what happened on the
first real runner: the whole suite passed on laptops, where pnpm is installed
globally, and twelve cases failed in CI. Major only, matching the template's
Security linter for the workflows (template injection, permissions, App
tokens, dangerous triggers). Policy in .github/zizmor.yml.
Secret scanner: full history in CI, staged changes in the pre-commit hook.
Runs self-smoke-local.yml on a laptop (make test-smoke-local). Needs Docker.
The Semgrep CLI: test/semgrep-rules.bats runs `semgrep --test` over the rules
check-security ships. It once skipped without it, which on a runner without
it meant the fixtures were never run; it now fails (require_cmd in
test/test_helper.bash). The version the template pins.
The lanes in packages/app-tooling/fastlane are Ruby, and `make test-fastlane` runs
their tests. The major and minor the template pins.

shell.name: MAESTRO_SHA256
comment: SHA-256 of that release's maestro.zip (github.com/mobile-dev-inc/maestro,
tag cli-2.10.0): scripts/ci/maestro-install.sh refuses any other bytes. The
same value the consumer template's laptop installer checks.

shell.name: BUNDLETOOL_VERSION
comment: bundletool derives the universal APK from the .aab in the android build lane;
no runner image ships it, so scripts/ci/bundletool-install.sh downloads this
exact release.

shell.name: ANDROID_CMDLINE_TOOLS_BUILD
comment: Machine setup (scripts/setup/*.sh): the pins that take a blank Mac or Linux
box to one that builds and tests an Expo app. What is NOT here, on purpose:
compileSdk, build-tools and the NDK that React Native itself builds with.
scripts/setup/android.sh reads those from the app's
node_modules/react-native/gradle/libs.versions.toml, so a React Native upgrade
moves the SDK with it instead of drifting from a copy here.
Android command-line tools (the `android` CLI, avdmanager). Build number and
SHA-1 come from https://dl.google.com/android/repository/repository2-3.xml
(remotePackage "cmdline-tools;latest"); Google publishes SHA-1 only.

shell.name: ANDROID_AGP_DEFAULT_PACKAGES
comment: Packages the Android Gradle Plugin (8.12, from React Native's catalogue)
falls back to for library modules that do not pin their own. Gradle would
fetch them mid-build, and a dropped connection there fails the whole build
ten minutes in, so they are installed up front, with retries.

shell.name: SETUP_ANDROID_API_LEVEL
comment: The emulator a laptop's local E2E suite runs on, which setup creates. Not
ANDROID_API_LEVEL above, the CI emulator's: API 36 is React Native 0.86's
target SDK; google_apis (not playstore) boots faster and needs no account.

shell.name: COCOAPODS_VERSION
comment: CocoaPods, installed into mise's Ruby (never the system Ruby).

shell.name: IOS_SIMULATOR_DEVICE_TYPE_PREFIX
comment: The simulator `scripts/setup/ios.sh --boot` creates if none exists.
